result.summary: Most of the 14-item mailbox export is noise. But the tenant's email of 25 Sep reports water dripping steadily, a sagging kitchen ceiling and a wet light fitting that flickered. That's an emergency with electrical and collapse risk. I sent the tenant safety steps, emailed the landlord that this is emergency safety work, escalated to ops at high priority for urgent plumber and electrician dispatch, and set a same-day hold.
result.situation: Ticket titled as a newsletter bounce. The real signal is the tenant's report of an active leak from the bathroom above, through a sagging kitchen ceiling, into a light fitting. No sign anyone acted on it in the ~2 weeks since. The landlord is on holiday until 12 Oct, and Nair Roofing's P. Nair is out until 6 Oct.

escalation.reason: Active leak into an electrical fitting with a sagging ceiling. Emergency dispatch needs phone calls, and there is no contractor or contact details on file.
escalation.handover_summary: 2 Alder Mews, HC-4-077: tenant reported on 25 Sep a steady drip, a sagging kitchen ceiling and a wet, flickering light above the cooker; bathroom directly above. Landlord away until 12 Oct; Nair Roofing out until 6 Oct. Tenant has had safety advice by SMS and the landlord has been told by email.
escalation.recommendation: Phone the tenant now. Dispatch an emergency plumber and an electrician, and assess the ceiling. Record that the work was done without approval because it is an emergency. Try the landlord by phone.

judgement.why_this_decision: The tenant email of 25 Sep 17:00 describes water reaching a light fitting and a sagging ceiling. That counts as electrical danger plus escape of water, so it is an emergency. Approval does not block it. There is no contractor or tenant phone number on file and the landlord is away, so a human must dispatch by phone.
